For states γ, γ′ of sizes R, R′ ≥ r0, log F(γ; v) F(γ′; v) ≤ C 1 + | log(R/R′ )|  . (3.2) 9 There is δ > 0 such that every F(γ; vew) is nonzero for |w| < δ. Its logarithm, continued from its real value at w = 0, has absolute value at most C log(2 + R). Moreover log F(γ; vew) F(γ; v) − log F(γ′; vew) F(γ′; v) ≤ C|w| 1 + | log(R/R′ )|  . (3.3) For two states of comparable size R, their positively tilted laws can be coupled so that their configurations agree inside a common surrounding primal-open circuit containing B(u, s), except with probability C(s/R)c, for r0 ≤ s ≤ R/C. Conditional on the common circuit, the common continuation has its circuit law tilted by v. Finally, let F≥h(γ; v) count only the eligible loops with Ru(ℓ) ≥ h. For comparable starts of size R, F≥ϵR(γ; v)/F≥ϵR(γ′; v) F(γ; v)/F(γ′; v) = 1 + o(1) (3.4) uniformly as ϵ ↓ 0 and ϵR → ∞.
